title: Dạ
summary: Use Dạ as a polite yes, a respectful opener, or a soft way to show you are listening.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Dạ is one of the most useful small words in Vietnamese. It can answer yes, show that you heard someone, soften the start of a sentence, or make a short reply sound respectful. Travelers should learn it as a polite response marker first, then choose Có, Không, Được, or Đúng when the answer itself needs to be clear.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Dạ when someone older, staff, a driver, or a local helper speaks to you and you want to answer politely before the main information.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The whole word is short, so the useful lesson is what it does in the conversation.

breakdown.english: respectful yes / I hear you / softens the answer

sections.title: Answer choices
sections.body: Dạ can come before an answer, but these words carry the answer itself.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it when a staff member asks a question, when an older person speaks first, when you are confirming that you heard instructions, or when you want to sound gentle before a short request. It works beautifully before Chào anh, Cảm ơn, or a yes/no answer.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Dạ does not replace every yes. If the person needs a clear answer, say Dạ first if you want, then add Có, Không, Được, or Đúng.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: These are natural next steps after a polite acknowledgment.
